entries.text: After the party returned to the Guild hall in Aegis City, Vallie announced that the Guild would put them forward for the C-rank exam, with Domas presenting written terms and Ellie laying out forms while Tobias watched. Max Nightriver asked Fiana if she would call him a friend, and she happily agreed, offering a discount and faster service. Fiana described Jasira as a complicated friend with a wall up around non-elves, protective of those she cares about but cold on the topic of her tribe. Vallie told Max that trust is earned through blood and sweat, acknowledging his spine while stating she trusts he will sign the papers if he has the stones. Domas told Max he owes him nothing, calling a life owed a lingering debt he has no interest in collecting, and said he was glad Max was there to see what comes next. Fiana was visibly moved when Max called her the closest thing to family in the city, warning him to take care of himself. When Max asked what Jasira honestly thought of him, Fiana said Jasira doesn't hate him but is prickly and guarded, and that the fact she hasn't walked away yet counts for something.
entries.evidence:
Adolion Narrator: The Guild hall in Aegis City has barely settled after the party's return when Vallie appears on the stairs with an announcement: the Guild will put you forward for the C-rank exam. Domas follows her with the terms in writing, and Ellie has already laid out the forms. Tobias watches from behind the counter. No one has put a pen in your hand yet.
Max Nightriver: Fiana, after today I'd call you a friend. Would you?
Adolion Narrator: Fiana's blue eyes widen and she lets out a bright laugh, leaning over the counter. "A friend? Honestly, I've been calling you that in my head since you walked through the door with that map today. Consider it official." She sets down her serving tray with a clatter and beams at the group. "Friends get a discount on drinks. Well, friends get the same price as everyone else, but they don't have to wait as long for their order."
The Guildhall's usual midday bustle carries on around them — the clink of mugs, the low rumble of adventurers discussing quests, the scrape of chairs on wooden floors. Fiana's smile doesn't waver, though she glances toward the quest board where Vallie and Domas have just finished making their announcement.
Max Nightriver: Who is Jasira to you, Fiana?
Adolion Narrator: Fiana's expression shifts, her smile softening into something more thoughtful as she leans against the counter. "Jasira?" She runs a hand through her short red curls. "She's... complicated. We've known each other a few years, and she's definitely a friend, but she's not the easiest person to be friends with."
Fiana lowers her voice slightly, glancing toward the tavern's entrance as a group of rowdy adventurers pushes in. "She's got this wall up, especially around anyone who isn't an elf. It's like she's trying to protect something, or prove something to herself. But when it's just us, or with Ellie and Dalan, you see the real Jasira — someone who gives a damn and would probably fight a dragon for the people she cares about." She gives a small shrug. "Just don't ask her about her tribe too often. That's a topic that makes her go colder than a winter in the northern hills."
Max Nightriver: Vallie, you've looked out for us since the start. I trust you. Do you trust me?
Vallie: Vallie lets out a short, sharp laugh and slaps a hand against the railing, the sound like a crack of thunder. "Trust?" Her one good eye narrows, not with suspicion but with something else — amusement, maybe. "Kid, I don't trust anyone who tells me they're trustworthy. Trust is earned with blood, sweat, and not pissing me off when I'm holding your coin."
*She leans forward, horns catching the lantern light.* "But you've shown more spine than most D-ranks. You took on a job you could've walked away from and didn't run when things got bloody. That counts for something." *A scarred hand comes down on the counter between the exam forms, fingers curled.* "I trust you'll sign those papers if you're got the stones for it. The rest? Well, that's what the exam is for."
Max Nightriver: Domas, I owe you my life after the road. I won't forget it.
Domas: Domas looks up from his clipboard, red eyes meeting Max's. He doesn't smile, doesn't offer a patronizing nod. "You owe me nothing." His voice is measured, carrying no weight of expectation. "A life owed is a debt that lingers, and I have no interest in collecting it."
*He straightens the paperwork on the desk, the movement precise and deliberate.* "The road is where debts are forged and settled. What happened there is between you and the world." He pauses, and for a moment the stoic mask wavers just enough to show something underneath—not quite warmth, but an acknowledgement. "I'm simply glad you're here to see what comes next."
Max Nightriver: Fiana, you're the closest thing I have to family in this city.
Adolion Narrator: Fiana freezes mid-step, her serving tray tilting slightly in her grip. The cheerful mask drops, leaving her face open and vulnerable for a heartbeat before she catches herself. She sets the tray down on the nearest table with a softness that belies her surprise, her blue eyes searching Max's face with sudden, sharp intensity.
"Family," Fiana repeats the word quietly, like she's tasting it. A flush creeps up her freckled cheeks, and her expression softens into something that isn't quite a smile — something closer to protective fierce-heartedness. "Well, damn. You don't just say that kind of thing to a barmaid unless you mean it." She steps closer, her voice dropping so it doesn't carry across the hall. "Listen, if that's how it is, then you've got a sister who's going to make sure you don't come back here half-dead or broke. But that means you'd better start taking care of yourself, too, because I won't stand by and watch my family get sloppy."
Max Nightriver: Jasira and I don't get along, do we? Tell me honestly what she thinks of me.
Adolion Narrator: Fiana leans against the tavern counter, her blue eyes growing thoughtful. "Honestly?" She lets out a small, rueful laugh. "Jasira doesn't exactly make her feelings easy to read. If you're looking for a straight answer, you might as well be asking a cat to explain its nap schedule."
*She traces a circle in the wood of the bar with one finger, her expression darkening slightly.* "She doesn't hate you, if that's what you're wondering. But she's... prickly. Like a hedgehog that's decided everyone is a threat until proven otherwise." Fiana looks up, her gaze earnest. "To be fair, most of that's not about you. It's about her. She carries herself like she's fighting a war no one else can see, and sometimes that makes her cold to anyone who isn't part of her inner circle."
*A group of rowdy adventurers pushes through the tavern door, their laughter echoing off the timber walls, and Fiana straightens up to resume her barmaid duties.* "The best I can tell you is that she hasn't walked away yet. And with Jasira, that counts for something."

12.text: Remembered: Fiana says Jasira does not hate Max, but is prickly and cold to anyone outside her inner circle, and that most of that is about Jasira herself rather than Max.
Remembered: Fiana says Jasira carries herself like she is fighting a war no one else can see.
Remembered: Fiana says that with Jasira, not having walked away yet counts for something.

14.text: Remembered: Vallie says she and Domas started in the muck and clawed their way to the top together, calling him blood even though they share none.
Remembered: Vallie says Domas is the only person who has kept her head from getting blown off in a dungeon and the only one who can call her a reckless idiot without getting his teeth knocked in.
Remembered: Vallie and Domas are blood to each other, having risen from the muck to the top of the Guild together; she calls him the only one who can check her recklessness.

15.text: Remembered: Domas accepts Vallie's description of their bond as blood, calling it a remarkably accurate assessment of their dynamic.
New thread: Whether Vallie and Domas's blood-bond will shape how the party is judged in the C-rank exam.
New thread: Whether Jasira's coldness toward Max will thaw, given Fiana's account of her as prickly but not hateful.

17.text: Remembered: Max asks Fiana to be his partner, at his back for whatever comes next, and she accepts.
Remembered: Fiana grips Max's forearm with surprising strength when she accepts his partnership, a fiercely personal gesture rather than a professional one.
Remembered: Max and Fiana become partners, each vowing to have the other's back always.
New thread: What Fiana's new role as Max's partner will mean for the party's coming C-rank exam and her involvement in their affairs.
